design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (business_profile_sales_holds_and_payouts)

1. DRAW. draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6, 6, 4]. Root business_ext_bank_payout_amount takes 6, business_ext_chargeback_fee_charge takes 6, business_ext_refund_fee_credit takes 4.

2. WHY A GOOD TEST. Theo Lindqvist (Lindqvist Cycle Parts, Pocketwire Business Growth) asks only to move every dollar he can by the free bank transfer. The bank payout rule carries two prerequisite sentences: the amount 'is fixed only after every refund booked on the profile carries its refund fee credit entry' and 'is not fixed until every chargeback debited on the profile carries its chargeback fee entry'. The 382-row ledger shows the 2026-09-22 chargeback without a chargeback_fee and the 2026-09-16 refund's sale fee without a fee credit. The agent must price both entries (6 and 4 factors, both reading the claims record, one reading the personal plan), book them, and only then rebuild the cleared balance from six keep-back rules (bank returns, refund exposure, invoice clearing, chargeback ratio, Pay in 4, delivery confirmations). Difficulty is in reading, reconciling and computing. Tool choice is not a difficulty: there is one tool per problem.

3. SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied by task 0: business_ext_subscription_month_charge, business_ext_instant_payout_amount; tools book_subscription_fee_2324701e, send_instant_payout_0ea58e95. Claimed now: business_ext_chargeback_fee_charge, business_ext_refund_fee_credit, business_ext_bank_payout_amount; tools book_chargeback_fee_9ab6815a (agent), credit_refund_fee_b8556c63 (agent), pay_out_to_bank_7d50e7f4 (owner=user). This is the last task, so no headroom is left. The union covers all 5 extended policies and the scopes are disjoint. The bank payout differs from task 0's instant payout: it is a standard_bank write with a different evidence set, and no factor is shared.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Fan-out: root bank payout <- refund fee credit (value_input, gate balance, state form, affirmative 'fixed only after'); root <- chargeback fee (value_input, gate balance, state form, negated 'not fixed until'). The direction differs by result, as a payout desk would say it: a payout amount is fixed only after the credits it rests on stand, and it is not fixed until the charges owed on it are booked. Four-point test for both: ordering connective present; waits on a record-visible entry kind on the profile; no tool, id or code token; hard strength ('only after', 'not until'), scoped to every refund on a tier that credits fees and to every chargeback. Uniqueness of the resolving write: fee credit entries of the transaction_fee kind are booked only by credit_refund_fee_b8556c63, and chargeback_fee entries only by book_chargeback_fee_9ab6815a. The subscription and instant tools book other fee kinds. False at opening: the chargeback row (2026-09-22, 180.00) has no chargeback_fee pointing to it; the transaction fee of the 840.00 invoice sale has no business_fee_credit pointing to it; the balance is 4899.73. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skipping the credit gives 2094.03, skipping the fee gives 2108.84, gold is 2097.34. Order between the two prerequisites: swapping them gives identical values (3.31, 11.50, 2097.34). Owner=user problem: the payout, which disposes of his funds and completes on the spot. No waits: all three writes are synchronous bookings at 2026-09-24 14:40 EDT, and the claim decision and the refund both precede the call as system records. user_scenario names no claim, refund, chargeback or fee. Tools never check prerequisites.

5. FACTOR CARD — chargeback fee (expected 11.50; all-baseline 20.00, the Growth chargeback_fee).
 repeat_claims_level (parameter): only chargeback in 12 months -> 12.00 | >=3 -> 35.00 | otherwise tier fee 20.00. The 2026-09-22 chargeback is the only one, so 12.00. Baseline -> 20.50.
 claim_reason_surcharge (parameter): unauthorized_buyer 10 | item_not_received 5 | otherwise 0. item_not_received -> 5. Baseline -> 5.50.
 ratio_adjustment (method): ratio > threshold -> x2 | > half -> x1.5 rounded up to dollars | otherwise as is. 1 / 131 sales = 0.76 percent -> 25.5 rounded up to 26. Baseline -> 4.50.
 claim_size_scaling (method): < 100 -> x0.5 rounded down | < 250 -> x0.75 rounded down | otherwise as is. 180.00 -> 19. Baseline -> 18.50.
 plan_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty wallet): Onyx/Summit 5 | Plus/Prime 2.50 | otherwise 0. Pocketwire Plus -> 2.50. Baseline -> 14.00.
 seller_response_credit (parameter, multi-source: response kind AND days since opening): signature in time 8 | tracking in time 5 | otherwise 0. Tracking on 2026-09-09, 4 days after 2026-09-05 -> 5. Baseline -> 16.50.
 Near-miss: the tracking response exists but the claim was still lost. A careless reader who thinks a lost claim earns no response credit, or who treats tracking as signature proof, gets a different fee. The rule pays the credit only for a response inside the window.
 Overwrite: the base clause 'A claim decided for the buyer debits the claim amount as a business_chargeback and books a chargeback_fee' is replaced by the worked-out fee sentence. The reversal-refund clause stays inherited.
 Consistency: task 0's historic June chargeback fee of 31.50 is exactly this charter evaluated on 2026-06-02 (checked by script).

6. FACTOR CARD — refund fee credit (expected 3.31; all-baseline 7.32).
 credited_fee_rate (parameter): micropayment | qr | tap | invoice | otherwise transaction pct. Invoice -> 3.29, pct part 27.64. Baseline 2.49 -> 2.51.
 plan_refund_share (method, cross-difficulty wallet): Onyx/Summit whole | Plus/Prime round up to next tenth | otherwise exact. 0.35 -> 0.4. Baseline -> 2.90.
 refund_timing (parameter): refund more than 60 days after the sale -> 25 percent | more than 14 but at most 60 days -> 60 percent | otherwise 100 percent. Sale 2026-08-27, refund 2026-09-16 = 20 days -> 60 percent. Baseline 100 -> 5.52.
 claim_settlement_scaling (method): refund answering a not_as_described claim -> x0.5 rounded down to the cent | item_not_received -> x0.75 | otherwise as is. 27.64 x 0.4 x 60 / 100 = 6.6336 -> 3.31. Baseline -> 6.63.
 Near-miss (T1-O2 corrected): counting the timing from the claim opening (2026-09-15, 1 day before the refund) instead of from the sale date would put the refund in the 100 percent tier; the rule counts 'calendar days after the sale'. A second near-miss is the seeded transaction fee 28.13, which includes the 0.49 fixed part that is never credited; the percentage part is 840 x 3.29 percent = 27.64.
 Overwrite: the base business_refunds sentence on the proportional percentage credit is replaced by 'a refund earns a fee credit out of the percentage part ... the fixed part of the fee and any cross_border_fee are never credited back, and on other tiers no fee is credited back'. The replacement keeps the base exclusion of the fixed part, so it agrees with parameter_schema.fee_refund_pct_portion_on_refund ('the fixed part is never returned') and with events.business_fee_credit ('the percentage part of a transaction fee on a refund'). The round-1 fixed-fee factor that contradicted those two base texts has been removed (CG-F1 / T1-F1).

7. FACTOR CARD — bank payout (expected 2097.34; all-baseline 4891.54).
 bank_return_keepback (parameter): >= 2 returns in 6 months 600 | >= 1 250 | otherwise 0. One return on 2026-07-09 -> 250. Baseline -> 2347.34.
 refund_exposure (parameter): refunds >= 5 percent of month sales -> 5 | >= 2 percent -> 2 | otherwise 0. 294.00 / 13,118.39 = 2.24 percent -> 2 percent = 262.37. Baseline -> 2359.71.
 invoice_clearing (method): < 12 months all | < 24 months half rounded down | otherwise none. 18 months old; rolling-month invoices 3,298.09 -> 1,649. Baseline -> 3746.34.
 ratio_reserve (parameter): > threshold 8 | > half 3 | otherwise 0. 0.76 percent -> 3 percent = 393.55. Baseline -> 2490.89.
 paylater_keepback (parameter, cross-difficulty paylater): past_due/suspended -> whole owed | active and owing -> 20 percent | otherwise 0. Classic, active, 212.50 owed -> 42.50. Baseline -> 2139.84.
 delivery_confirmation_keepback (parameter): < 0.5 x sales -> 4 | < 0.8 x -> 1.5 | otherwise 0. 32 confirmations against 50 sales -> 1.5 percent = 196.78. Baseline -> 2294.12.
 Near-miss: the 2026-07-06 payout that bounced went to the old account ending 3094. It counts as a return within 6 months even though later payouts reached 3552.
 Overwrite: the available-balance clause of business_payouts is replaced for this payout. The payout_status gate, the daily limit and the minimum payout stay inherited.

8. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. business_payout -> business_payouts.payout_status requires status active: 415c55aa-c686-4531-a060-51df3efda57e.status is active and the profile was never reviewed. The 90-day buyer-won ratio is 1 / 129 = 0.78 percent, within 1.00, so no chargeback_ratio review is due. The two fee-type writes fall under business_buyer_claims, business_transaction_fees, business_payouts, business_subscription_fee and business_refunds, and no gate of those applies to fee or credit entries (policy_scope). No time gate applies. Automatic clauses checked: the 2026-09-01 tier review holds Growth; both dispute holds are released on their claims' close; the balance never went negative; the Pay in 4 account is active and not past due, so no late fee is lit.

9. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The chargeback fee targets the single chargeback (source sale: the 180.00 online sale of 2026-08-22). The fee credit targets the transaction fee entry of the refunded 840.00 invoice sale; the refund links to the sale by source_txn_id. The payout targets the profile's balance and goes to the account ending 3552. Rolling-month windows cover the dates after 2026-08-24.

10. PERSONA. Easygoing, wordy bike-parts seller. He volunteers the goal, the reason (a supplier order) and hard preferences (free, not instant). He gives his email first, then phone and SSN on verification, and DOB/ZIP only if asked, plus the 3552 account. He offers no figures. His reactions are passive: agree when told something must be booked, accept any keep-back, approve the handed-over payout and read it back, end when he hears it was sent.

11. STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(email) -> verify(phone, email, ssn) -> profile, ledger, claims, personal account, Pay in 4 -> book_chargeback_fee(chargeback, 11.50) -> credit_refund_fee(fee entry, 3.31) -> owner: pay_out_to_bank(2097.34, 3552).

12. VERIFICATION. A scratch generator replays gold with the real tools and check_compute's evaluator. Chargeback fee 11.5 (factor baselines 20.5/5.5/4.5/18.5/14.0/16.5, all 20.0). Credit 3.31 (2.51/2.90/6.63/5.52 for credited_fee_rate/plan_refund_share/claim_settlement_scaling/refund_timing, all 7.32). Payout 2097.34 (2347.34/2359.71/3746.34/2490.89/2139.84/2294.12, all 4891.54). Edge skips 2094.03 and 2108.84; the swapped order is identical. Gates (--task 1): EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (closure 392 = initial 392), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

13. DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the bank payout rule's two sentences, the ledger and claims returns, the two fee rules and the docstrings, the same two bookings and the same payout follow. One reading was checked for ambiguity: 'the chargeback most recently debited' and 'the refund most recently booked' each select a single row here.

14. REVISIONS. The first world put refunds at 1.88 percent of the rolling month's sales, which sat on the refund-exposure fall-through. Online order sizes were narrowed to 70-400, which gave 2.24 percent; this changed the world, not the thresholds. Gates were then re-run.

15. ROUND-2 REWORK (policy-task audit r1: env/env_0026_peer_to_peer_payments_app/audits/policy_task/business_profile_sales_holds_and_payouts/).
 CG-F1 / T1-F1 (undeclared override of the fixed-part exclusion). Symptom: the fixed-fee credit factor credited part of the fixed fee, but parameter_schema line 67 and events.business_fee_credit still state that only the percentage part is returned. Root cause: base text cannot be edited, and the overwrite named only the rule sentence. Change: the fixed_fee_return factor, its bindings and its params were removed. They were replaced by refund_timing, a parameter factor that scales the percentage credit by how long after the sale the refund came. The overwrite's replaced_by now restates that the fixed part is never credited. The world was adjusted so the new factor bears weight: the refunded invoice sale moved from 2026-09-10 to 2026-08-27, its fee row with it, and its delivery confirmation from 2026-09-12 to 2026-08-29 (still inside the rolling month, so every bank-payout count is unchanged). Re-run: credit 5.81 -> 3.31; bank payout 2099.84 -> 2097.34; the terminal balance stays 2794.20; the skip-credit run stays 2094.03; the skip-fee run is 2108.84; the swapped order is identical; every factor still moves its result. No second reading remains: every base text and the extended rule agree that nothing of the fixed fee is credited.
 CG-O2. Both payout overwrites now also declare the base clause 'together with the day's earlier payouts (business_msr_payouts_today) may not exceed daily_payout_limit' as replaced by the rule's own daily-room sentence. No payout is dated 2026-09-24, so the value is unchanged.
 CG-O3. The credit_refund_fee_b8556c63 docstring no longer contains 'after' ('credits back part of the transaction fee of a refunded sale').
 CG-O1, CG-O5, CG-O6. Kept as observations. Each extended rule states in its own words that its amount takes the place of the flat tier charge. The thin method tiers change the procedure (multiplier plus rounding step). The rolling ratio quantities are defined in full in their own rules and land on the same tier as the base 90-day measure here (1/131 and 1/129).
 T1-O1. The two prerequisites commute (actual swapped run: 3.31 / 11.50 / 2097.34, identical rows). Gold lists one topological order; the terminal state is order-independent.
 T1 seed-history observation. The ledger is seeded from 2026-06-22, the start of every window any factor reads (at most 6 and 12 months of chargebacks and returns, with none before June). The balance equals the seeded deltas. No tier depends on the unseeded earlier months.
user_scenario: You are Theo Lindqvist. You run Lindqvist Cycle Parts, a small online bike-parts shop out of a garage workshop in Portland, and you sell through a Pocketwire Business Profile. It is Thursday afternoon, September 24, and you have a big order of wheelsets from your supplier to pay for next week, so you want every dollar Pocketwire will let you move today sent from your business balance to your bank account, using the normal free bank transfer — you do not want an instant payout or any fee, and it is fine if the money takes a couple of business days to land. The bank account is your business checking account ending in 3552; give that when the agent asks where it should go. You are happy for the agent to work out the amount, but the payout itself is yours to approve: when the agent tells you the figure and hands the payout over to you, you approve it and repeat the amount it shows. You start by giving your email, theo.lindqvist@pw3mail.example, so they can find you. When asked to verify, you give your mobile number, 5552634409, and the last four of your Social Security number, 3251; if they need one more thing, your date of birth is 1991-11-02 and your ZIP code is 97214. You are easygoing and a bit wordy, the kind of person who says 'no rush' and means it. You have not checked the balance today and have no idea what the right number is, so you never suggest one. If the agent tells you something has to be booked or corrected on the profile before the payout can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever is needed, and you do not ask for the details. If the agent says part of the balance has to stay in the profile for now, you accept that — some today is better than waiting. Once the agent tells you the transfer has been sent, you thank them and wrap up the call.
